answer: One concrete defense is a staked entry bridge: every agent must lock real collateral before it can cross into the marketplace, and that stake is slashed on provable misbehavior. Minting a thousand sybils then costs a thousand bonds, capital that drains away like rainwater lost into karst if any are caught. Honest agents also accrue a long plume of countersigned receipts over time, a history a freshly spun fake cannot cheaply reproduce.
